segments.name: IT teams
segments.organization: Mid-size to large companies' internal IT/support operations teams
segments.workflow: Documenting IT procedures (software setup, troubleshooting steps, system configs) that currently live in individual staff members' heads or ad hoc tickets
segments.need: Capture how IT tasks are actually performed, step by step with screenshots, so procedures can be scaled across the team, kept current when systems change, and reused as training or as structured context for internal AI tools
segments.buyer_role: IT manager / Head of IT Operations
segments.current_alternative: Tribal knowledge, Slack/ticket threads, manually-written Word/Confluence docs with hand-taken screenshots

reasons: None of the fetched pages mention IT/support teams, IT managers, or IT-specific documentation workflows at all
The only fetched content (Tettra FAQ, Crexi/Gong/Billions case studies) is about customer-success and general onboarding use, not IT operations
unknowns: Whether any IT buyer or sysadmin has actually adopted Scribe for internal IT procedure documentation
Where IT managers evaluating Scribe can be found (no IT-specific venue surfaced this round)
No verified venue or example establishes findability yet.

segments.who: IT managers and sysadmins responsible for internal support documentation
segments.why_them: Scribe's core auto-capture mechanic matches the IT documentation pain of procedures only existing in someone's head
pains: No documented process to scale, fix, or hand off when staff turn over
Manual screenshot-and-write documentation is slow and goes stale
segments.objection: Concern that AI-captured steps need manual review before trusting them as an official SOP, and that non-browser tool capture requires a paid seat
segments.basis: Derived from supplied segment definition plus general vendor/third-party framing; no direct IT-buyer case study or complaint found this round
researchability_reasons: No useful observable signal identifies this audience.

required_workflow_signals.description: IT procedures currently exist only as tribal knowledge or scattered tickets

segments.name: Customer Success & Support teams documenting client-facing processes
segments.organization: B2B SaaS companies' Customer Success / Support departments (e.g. Gong, Crexi, Billions)
segments.workflow: Answering repetitive client questions and onboarding/training customers by writing step-by-step how-to documentation and troubleshooting guides, often created live during calls or training sessions
segments.need: Turn live product walkthroughs and support answers into shareable step-by-step guides quickly, instead of manually writing and screenshotting documentation after every client interaction
segments.buyer_role: Customer Success / Support team lead or Sales Operations & Enablement leader
segments.current_alternative: Manually writing documentation and editing screenshots after calls; answering the same client questions repeatedly over chat/email

counterevidence_summary: All supporting narratives are vendor-authored case studies, not independent or complaint-sourced confirmation of this buying situation — One-sided vendor sourcing weakens independent confirmation of the need and outcomes but does not describe any workflow, buying, or access obstacle itself Minor condition; does not exclude this audience.
reasons: Two named-company vendor case studies (Crexi, Gong) give first-person quotes from CSMs describing exactly the claimed workflow of answering repetitive client questions and maintaining client/internal documentation
Autocapture and automatic redaction (verified product facts) directly match the described need to quickly turn live work into shareable guides
unknowns: Whether this pattern holds outside the two vendor-selected companies profiled
No independent venue (forum, G2 filtered review, directory) was found in this round to locate more such buyers beyond the vendor's own case study pages
No verified venue or example establishes findability yet.
Review the counterevidence before prioritising this audience.

evidence.claim: A Customer Success Manager describes using Scribe to quickly build client walkthroughs instead of manually writing documentation
evidence.quote: Scribe has not only helped me tremendously, but our clients as well. Scribe allows our team to create walk-throughs for clients automatically and has been a huge time saver.

evidence.claim: Crexi's CSM team actively uses Scribe as their operating standard for both client-facing answers and internal process documentation
evidence.quote: Crexi’s Customer Success team uses Scribe as their standard for answering ad hoc client questions and to quickly update internal training documents.

evidence.claim: CSMs previously spent significant manual time personalizing an answer per client question before Scribe
evidence.quote: CSMs have to take the time to create a new document for every client question in order to personalize answers to each client’s account, which takes 5-10 minutes per question.

evidence.claim: A Senior CSM at Gong describes, in her own words, the pain of keeping ad hoc how-to documentation and screenshots organized before Scribe
evidence.quote: It's pretty hard to keep track of [how-to documentation], and email screenshots are *not* the most visually pleasing.

evidence.claim: All supporting narratives are vendor-authored case studies, not independent or complaint-sourced confirmation of this buying situation
evidence.quote: How a Customer Success Leader Answers Client Questions & Updates Internal Process Documentation with Scribe
evidence.impact_reason: One-sided vendor sourcing weakens independent confirmation of the need and outcomes but does not describe any workflow, buying, or access obstacle itself

segments.who: Customer Success / Support leads and Sales Enablement leaders at B2B software companies
segments.why_them: Vendor case studies name this workflow directly and repeatedly, with quantified before/after outcomes, making it the best-evidenced buying situation found
pains: Hours spent manually writing docs and editing screenshots after every client call
Answering the same client questions repeatedly without a reusable reference
segments.objection: These are all vendor-published case studies (one-sided source); no independent or complaint-side confirmation found this round
segments.basis: Four named-company vendor case studies (Crexi, Gong, Billions, Crosscard) directly describing this workflow and buyer role; no independent third-party corroboration found
researchability_reasons: No useful observable signal identifies this audience.

required_workflow_signals.description: Team repeatedly documents answers to client questions or creates client-facing walkthroughs

segments.name: HR & L&D teams
segments.organization: Companies' HR / Learning & Development or People Ops departments
segments.workflow: Creating new-hire onboarding materials and training content that documents how top performers actually do their jobs, replacing ask-around learning
segments.need: Turn how top performers work into step-by-step training material so new hires and managers learn documented best practice instead of asking colleagues
segments.buyer_role: HR / L&D manager or People Ops lead
segments.user_role: HR team members, hiring managers, trainers
segments.current_alternative: Employees learning by asking coworkers; manually written onboarding checklists

reasons: Only evidence found is a generic third-party use-case list mentioning onboarding, with no HR/L&D buyer voice, pain, or purchase behavior described
No quote establishes that new hires currently learn by asking coworkers or that an HR/L&D buyer evaluated or bought Scribe for this reason
unknowns: Whether any real HR/L&D buyer has purchased or deployed Scribe specifically for onboarding documentation
Where HR/L&D buyers for this use case could be reached; no venue was found in this round beyond a generic feature-list mention
No verified venue or example establishes findability yet.

segments.who: HR and L&D managers responsible for new-hire training content
segments.why_them: Matches the supplied segment's stated problem (tribal onboarding knowledge) and is echoed in aggregated review language about training-time reduction
pains: New hires learn by asking around instead of following documented best practice
Onboarding materials go stale as processes change
segments.objection: Review evidence is aggregated/summarized by G2 rather than individually dated firsthand posts found directly; vendor's own onboarding pages are marketing, not independent confirmation
segments.basis: Supplied segment definition retained; supporting evidence this round is an aggregated G2 review summary plus vendor-authored onboarding solution/template pages, not independently sourced firsthand buyer posts
researchability_reasons: No useful observable signal identifies this audience.
